chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hurz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'While Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was sitting in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) one day, he raised his head to him and said: O Father.' He said: 'At your service, O my son.'

He said: 'What is the reward for one who comes to you after your death as a visitor, seeking only your visitation?' He said: 'O my son, whoever comes to me after my death as a visitor, seeking only my visitation, will have Paradise. And whoever comes to your father after his death as a visitor, seeking only his visitation, will have Paradise. And whoever comes to you after your death as a visitor, seeking only your visitation, will have Paradise.'

key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service / Here I am

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of an Imam with the intention of visitation?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the theological basis for Ziyarat al-A’immah by linking the visitation of the Prophet, Ali, and Husayn directly to the reward of Paradise. It highlights the unique spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt, where visiting their graves is not merely a commemorative act but a means of drawing near to God through their intercession and presence.
